passage: Yash and Nilesh had been best friends since school in their small town. But since Nilesh came back from the city after what happened there, things were strange. Nilesh cancelled their Sunday cricket without a reason. When Yash clapped him on the back at the tea stall, Nilesh flinched and snapped, "Don't!" Yash walked home hurt and confused. What had he done? He wanted to ask what happened in the city. Everyone in the town was asking. But he remembered his cousin saying, "Pushing people to talk can make it worse." So the next evening he sat beside Nilesh on the temple steps and said, "I won't ask about it. Just tell me what helps, and what doesn't." Nilesh was quiet a long time. "Don't come up behind me. And don't stop inviting me, even if I say no." "Done," said Yash. The following Sunday, he sent the cricket invite again.

qa.q: Where did Yash sit beside Nilesh the next evening?
qa.a: On the temple steps.

qa.q: How did Yash feel after Nilesh snapped at the tea stall?
qa.a: He felt hurt and confused, wondering what he had done.

qa.q: What choice did Yash make instead of asking about the city?
qa.a: He promised not to ask about it and asked what helps and what doesn't, then followed Nilesh's answer.

qa.q: How might Nilesh feel when Yash sends the cricket invite again?
qa.a: He may feel cared for and not pushed, knowing his friend is still there at his own pace.

grounding: It shows a friend confused when a survivor pulls away or reacts strongly, who asks what helps, respects his pace and does not push for details.

passage: In their Lisbon apartment, Kwame came home and hugged Lucia from behind as she washed the dishes. She screamed and dropped a plate. Then she stood trembling, apologising over and over. Kwame's heart sank. Over the past months she'd cancelled dinners with his friends and sometimes stared past him as if she wasn't there. He'd started to wonder if it was him. He picked up the broken pieces. Then he sat at the table, a little distance away. "I'm sorry I startled you. You don't have to explain. What helps you?" Lucia wiped her eyes. "Tell me when you're coming near. Say my name first. And don't ask me about it, not yet. I'm talking about it with my therapist." "Okay," said Kwame. "Your pace." The next evening he called "Lucia, I'm home" from the door before he came in.

qa.q: What did Kwame call from the door the next evening?
qa.a: Lucia, I'm home.

qa.q: What had Kwame started to wonder, and why?
qa.a: His heart sank; he felt hurt and unsure, wondering if the problem was him, because Lucia had been cancelling dinners and seeming far away.

qa.q: Which of Kwame's choices helped create safety?
qa.a: He apologised, sat a little distance away, didn't ask for details and asked what helps, then followed her answer.

qa.q: How does Lucia experience being hugged from behind?
qa.a: It startles and frightens her so much she screams and trembles, even though it is Kwame.

grounding: It shows someone close to a survivor, confused when a survivor pulls away and reacts strongly, who asks what helps, respects her pace and does not push for details.

passage:
Week one: Since the bus accident, Shankar had cancelled plans with Lakshmi four times. When she hugged him from behind at the canteen, he flinched and snapped, "Don't." Lakshmi walked home confused and hurt. Had she done something?
Week two: Lakshmi didn't push. She texted, "I don't need details. What helps you right now?" He replied an hour later: "Just being around. No surprises. No questions about it."
Week four: They sat by the lake in silence, her in front of him where he could see her. After a long time Shankar said, "Some days the brakes screech in my head." Lakshmi just said, "Thank you for telling me." She didn't ask more. He leaned his shoulder against hers.

qa.q: How many times had Shankar cancelled plans in week one?
qa.a: He had cancelled plans four times.

qa.q: How did Lakshmi feel after Shankar snapped at the canteen?
qa.a: She felt confused and hurt, wondering if she had done something wrong.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi do that created safety for Shankar?
qa.a: She stopped pushing, asked what helps, avoided surprises and questions, and simply thanked him when he shared, without asking for details.

qa.q: How might Shankar feel when Lakshmi sits where he can see her?
qa.a: He may feel safer and calmer, which is why he eventually leans his shoulder against hers.

grounding: Shows a friend confused when a survivor pulls away and reacts strongly, who creates safety through patience, asking what helps and respecting his pace.

passage: "Eshaan, you're confused because your friend Kabir keeps pushing you away since the accident? Let your Dadu tell you. When I was twenty, my best friend Salim survived a fire at the mill where we both worked. After, he stopped coming to chai. Once I slapped his back and he nearly hit me. I was hurt. I thought, after all these years, this is how he treats me? Then my father said, 'Asif, don't ask him what happened. Ask him what helps.' So I did. Salim said, 'Just sit with me. Don't talk about the mill.' For months, we sat on the ghat steps every evening, not talking. One day he told me everything himself. Patience, beta. Let him set the pace."

qa.q: Where did Asif and Salim sit every evening?
qa.a: On the ghat steps.

qa.q: How did young Asif feel when Salim nearly hit him?
qa.a: He felt hurt and confused, thinking his friend was treating him badly after years of friendship.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Asif's story?
qa.a: His father told him to ask what helps rather than what happened, and Asif followed Salim's lead and waited patiently.

qa.q: How might Salim have felt when Asif simply sat with him?
qa.a: Salim may have felt safe and accepted, which let him eventually share everything himself.

grounding: An elder recalls feeling confused when a friend who survived a fire pulled away, and learning that patience, asking what helps and respecting pace create safety.

passage: The train home for Diwali was packed, and the fan above their berth rattled. Kiran had been looking forward to this trip with Tushar for weeks. But when the brakes screeched outside a station, Tushar went rigid, then turned to the window and didn't answer for an hour. Since the crash in March, Kiran never knew what would set him off. Kiran felt shut out and confused. Instead of asking what was wrong, Kiran quietly asked, "Do you want me to talk, or just sit?" "Just sit," Tushar said. Kiran passed him the earphones and sat close, not touching. Near midnight, Tushar said, "Thanks for not asking." Kiran nodded. "Whenever you want. Or never. Your call."

qa.q: What did Kiran pass to Tushar?
qa.a: Kiran passed him the earphones.

qa.q: How did Kiran feel when Tushar turned to the window?
qa.a: Kiran felt shut out and confused, not knowing what would set him off.

qa.q: What did Kiran do that respected Tushar's pace?
qa.a: Kiran asked what would help, sat close without touching, offered earphones and made clear he never had to share details.

qa.q: How might Tushar feel when Kiran says it's his call?
qa.a: Tushar may feel respected and safe, knowing he won't be pushed to talk about the crash.

grounding: Shows a companion confused when a survivor pulls away on a crowded train, creating safety through patience, asking what helps and not pushing for details.

passage:
Seema came up behind Nandini at the Andheri bus stop and put a hand on her shoulder. Nandini spun round, pushed her away and stood shaking.
"Sorry, sorry," Seema said, stunned. They had been friends since school.
Later that week Nandini cancelled their movie plan and stopped replying. Seema felt confused and a little hurt. What had she done?
She didn't push. On Sunday she texted, "I'm not asking about anything. I just want to know what helps you."
Nandini replied that evening. "Don't come up behind me. Tell me before you touch me. And please don't ask about last year. I'm working on it with my counsellor."
"Done," Seema wrote. "I'll wait till you're ready, or forever."
The next week Nandini met her for chai. Seema said, "Hi, I'm right here," before sitting down. Nandini smiled.

qa.q: Where was Nandini when Seema put a hand on her shoulder?
qa.a: At the Andheri bus stop.

qa.q: How did Seema feel when Nandini cancelled and stopped replying?
qa.a: She felt confused and a little hurt, wondering what she had done.

qa.q: Which of Seema's choices created safety?
qa.a: Not pushing for details, asking what helps, respecting Nandini's pace and following her requests, like announcing herself before sitting down.

qa.q: How might Nandini see Seema after the Sunday text?
qa.a: She probably feels relieved and trusts Seema more, admiring how she respects her pace without asking questions.

grounding: Seema is confused when Nandini pulls away and reacts strongly, and patience, asking what helps and respecting her pace without pushing for details create safety.
